prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — do you want a quick list of specific contractors, or would you prefer a short plan to find and vet reliable local pros yourself? If you want names, tell me the type of work (kitchen, full remodel, roof, plumbing, electrical, general repairs) and your timeline/budget and I’ll tailor recommendations.

Meanwhile, here are practical, local-first steps and what to check so you get a reliable contractor in Joplin, MO.

Where to look
- Joplin Area Chamber of Commerce business directory (locally vetted member businesses).  
- Google Maps and Yelp for local contractors with recent reviews.  
- Better Business Bureau (BBB) for complaints and ratings.  
- Angi, Houzz, Thumbtack, and Nextdoor for local pros and project photos/reviews.  
- Joplin city Building Services / permit office to confirm who gets permits and code compliance.  
- Local Facebook community groups — people often post recent referrals.

How to vet candidates
- Ask for proof of insurance (general liability and workers’ comp) and verify the policy.  
- Confirm licenses for trades that require them (electrical, plumbing, HVAC) with state or city authorities.  
- Get at least 3 written bids that itemize labor, materials, timelines, and allowances.  
- Request three local references (recent projects) and call them — ask about quality, timeliness, and change-order handling.  
- Check BBB and online reviews for patterns (not just a single review).  
- Verify they’ll obtain required permits and do inspections.

Questions to ask every contractor
- Are you licensed/insured? Can I see certificates?  
- Can you provide 3 local references from similar jobs? May I visit a recent job?  
- Who will manage the project day-to-day? Will subcontractors be used?  
- What is the estimated start date and completion date? What can delay it?  
- Detailed payment schedule (never pay full amount up front).  
- How do you handle change orders and unexpected problems?  
- Do you provide a written warranty for materials and workmanship?

Contract & payment tips
- Get everything in writing: scope, materials, brand/model numbers, timeline, payment schedule, warranty, cleanup, and lien release language.  
- Typical safe payment schedule: deposit (10–20%) to schedule, progress payments tied to milestones, final payment after inspection and lien waivers.  
- Avoid paying cash-only or large upfront sums.  
- Require proof that subcontractors are insured or have the contractor’s coverage.

Red flags
- No written contract or unwillingness to sign one.  
- Demands for full payment up front or cash-only.  
- Vague scope or prices that are much lower than other bids.  
- Poor or nonexistent references, many unresolved BBB complaints, or a history of lawsuits.

If you want, I can:
- Compile a short list of Joplin-area contractors (I’ll need the project type).  
- Draft an email or message template you can send to multiple contractors.  
- Provide a bid-comparison worksheet template to evaluate offers.

Which would you like next?
